title: MVC, MVP and MVVM: where each one makes sense

videos.script: Every program with a screen does three jobs. It keeps the rules. It shows the state. And it takes what the person typed or clicked. {{jobs}} Put all three in one loop and it works, for a while. Then somebody wants the same desk on a web page, and the rules have to be copied into it. {{tangled}} This lesson pulls the three jobs apart, in three different ways. {{three}} First MVC, the oldest, from Smalltalk at the end of the seventies. A controller reads the keyboard, a model keeps the rules, and a view redraws itself when the model changes. {{mvc}} Then the version every web framework ships, where a route is the controller and a template is the view. {{server}} Then MVP, where the view becomes so thin that a test can stand in for it. {{mvp}} And MVVM, where the screen binds itself to properties and redraws on its own. {{mvvm}} All four run in your terminal, on the loan desk of the library, and all four share one model file that never changes. By the end you can look at a screen and say which of them it needs, or whether it needs any. {{choosing}}
